what_the_class_is: The reverb as a whole: the mono sum of the inputs through the pre-delay ladder, four loops each with the damping pole on its line's input, summed into a pair of series all-passes a side, then the balance, level and tone stages. The loops' loss a pass at the power-on Time is set so the 500 Hz band decays as the decay record read it at the power-on setting.

era.when: Mid nineteen-nineties, a custom fixed-point DSP running its effects at 32 kHz with a small control processor beside it.
what_that_implies: A reverb is a handful of circular buffers read back into themselves, each read scaled and added to what is written, because a loop costs one read, one multiply and one add however long its buffer is.
Whether the loops feed only themselves or each other is a question of which reads each write adds, and costs the same either way once the matrix is a set of signs.
A gated reverb is cheapest as a run of reads of one buffer with fixed weights, which ends exactly where its last read is and needs no detector.
Times, levels and corners are tables indexed by the byte, as the classes that read them closed on; a whole-type model borrows those tables rather than fitting its own.
era.would_be_wrong_if: The tail of a struck note came back with a density or a stereo spread no four-loop network or sixteen-read run can give, or its level at the Time or Gate Time settings nothing here was built on fell off other than the law each candidate states.

candidates.reading: The four loops are apart: each line is fed its own return only, a parallel comb bank. The Time byte is a loss a pass that falls by an eighth of its power-on value a step towards 128.
candidates.predicts: Discrete, regularly spaced early returns at each loop's length that thicken only through the all-passes; a tail of about a quarter second at Time 0 and eight times longer at 127 than at 120.

candidates.reading: The four loops are apart: each line is fed its own return only, a parallel comb bank. The Time byte is a decay time proportional to the byte, nothing at 0.
candidates.predicts: Discrete, regularly spaced early returns at each loop's length that thicken only through the all-passes; no tail past one pass of each loop at Time 0, and at 127 a tail six percent longer than at 120.

candidates.reading: The four loops are coupled: each line is fed every loop's return through an orthogonal four-by-four matrix. The Time byte is a loss a pass that falls by an eighth of its power-on value a step towards 128.
candidates.predicts: Returns that multiply with every pass, each loop feeding the others, so the tail is dense sooner; a tail of about a quarter second at Time 0 and eight times longer at 127 than at 120.

what_no_candidate_here_predicts: Any Type but the one the type powers up in. The page names the six by room size and no reading gives a length or a decay for any of them, so every candidate draws Stage2 alone and leaves the other five, and the value past the list that reads as Room1, undrawn.
Whether the damping claim, closed on the stereo delay and checked on the mod delay, reaches this type's HF Damp byte: it is carried here unmeasured, one pole on each line's input inside its loop.
Whether the Time byte's law is either of the two here: each has one anchor, the power-on setting, and the other end of the byte is the law's own.
Anything at the addresses the page does not print: no node reads them, so every candidate renders them as the power-on state.
How the inputs are summed onto the line: half of each here; no reading fixed it.

The lengths of the loops and all-passes, the all-pass gain of 0.7 and how the wet paths are scaled: no measurement here fixes any of them, and a waveform subtraction fits one gain over the whole take.
